q: Warm-up 1. A verb of the pattern ʾaCCeC (e.g. ʾaqreb) belongs to which stem?
opts: The Paael doubles the middle letter and has no ʾa-.

opts: The Paael here is factitive, not just intensive.

q: Warm-up 5. How do you tell a Paael participle from a Peal participle?
opts: The Paael has the m- prefix (mqaddeš); the Peal has none (kāteb).
The Peal has the m- prefix; the Paael has none.
The Paael ends in -ā; the Peal does not.
They look the same; only context tells.

opts: These are I-Alaph roots, but regular in pattern.

q: In the story, to whom did the guards go?
opts: They went to report on him.
They report what happened at the gate.

q: What do the guards claim they saw and heard?
opts: A man who said an evil word
A light from God at the gate
The king's anger follows their report.

q: How did the king react to the news?
opts: He became very angry (ragīz ṭāb) and ordered the man brought to him.
He went to the gate himself.
He has the guards bring Yukhannan.
The past would be the perfect.
Root ḥ-z-y, Peal perfect 1 c.sg.: 'I saw'
Root ḥ-z-y, Peal perfect 3 m.sg.: 'he saw'
The final ܬ is a suffix.
Root ʾ-t-y, Peal perfect 3 m.sg.: 'he came'
Root ʾ-t-y, Peal perfect 1 c.sg.: 'I came'
Root y-h-b, Peal perfect 3 m.pl.: 'they gave'
Root y-h-b, Peal perfect 3 m.sg.: 'he gave'
The final ܘ is a suffix.

q: Exercise 2. Which list gives the Peal perfect of ʾ-m-r for 'I said, we said, you (m.sg.) said, they (m.) said'?
opts: The first and third are swapped: 1 c.sg. is ʾemret.
We saw the light of God in the gate.
They saw the light of God in the gate.
We see the light of God at the door.
The light of God saw us at the gate.

q: Exercise 4. Which is the best Syriac for 'The evil king saw the man'?
opts: Correct: VSO, with l- marking the direct object.
That says the evil man saw the king.
